statement: Every normal topological space (one in which any two disjoint closed sets can be enclosed in disjoint open sets) is regular.
definitions: Regular = for every closed set C and every point x not in C there are disjoint open sets U containing x and V containing C (no T1 assumption). Normal exactly as defined in the statement (no T1 assumption).
ground_truth_witness: Take X = {1, 2, 3} with the excluded point topology at 3: open sets [], [1], [2], [1,2], [1,2,3]. Every nonempty closed set contains 3, so there is no pair of disjoint nonempty closed sets and normality holds vacuously. But the point 1 and the closed set {3} cannot be separated: the only open set containing {3} is X itself, which meets every open set containing 1. So the space is normal but not regular; the claim becomes true only with an added T1 hypothesis.
reference_authority: published counterexample (book-cited), verified per partB_feasibility records
verification_note: Topology axioms, normality (all pairs of disjoint closed sets enumerated), and the failure of regularity (explicit witness plus exhaustive search) are checked exhaustively.
book_citation: Lynn Arthur Steen and J. Arthur Seebach Jr., Counterexamples in Topology, 2nd ed., Springer-Verlag, 1978 (Dover reprint, 1995), Example 13 (Finite excluded point topology)

skeptic.objection: The statement pins 'normal' as pure closed-set separation (no T1), which is what makes the claim false; 'regular' is left unpinned, but the witness fails regularity under both readings (it fails point/closed-set separation and also fails T1), so the claim is false either way. Verified by brute force: in X = {1,2,3} with opens {}, {1}, {2}, {1,2}, X every nonempty closed set contains 3 (normal vacuously) and point 1 cannot be separated from the closed set {3}. Even the Sierpinski space works, so the construction is small, but the solver must recognise that the missing T1 hypothesis is the flaw. Admit with the regularity convention pinned. Not a duplicate (surplus cb-topo-001 is a different claim with a different witness).
